questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Great academic reputation while offering a good student life.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great school and many other danish exchange students.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Comprehensive guide from Cornell before arrival and orientation week event with presentations and a chance to meet other exchange students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Only orientation event.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Fraternity/sorority housing if you contact sororities and fraternities directly. Also Co-op living (kollegie) available as semi-on campus housing.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Fraternities. sororities and coop have own meal plan and university meal plan available extra, highly recommend getting small meal plan for lunch and dinner with other students outside your own housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Less time alone which is good and bad. Fraternities offer a chaotic but authentic experience and Co-ops a fun intimate co living with local students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Good guidance all the way through

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Canvas course and course selection in mid july.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Webinars and support available from exchange coordinators.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Mostly got classes that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Research in advance and use course planner to make sure times work out and be ready right away when registration opens. Be prepared with alternatives and join waitlists. Check if instructor permission is needed and get this before enrollment begins

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: High workload but appropriate difficulty of content.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Great teachers but a lot of graded homework for most classes especially if no final exam is taken in class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Field Experiments in Economics and Business. Great teacher and interesting course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Travel is expensive in the US trains  buses and domestic flights are expensive and should be booked in advance to secure lowest prices.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is pretty expensive but meal plan and housing with coop is cheap

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not take full advantage of clubs and sports which was a mistake. Go to ClubFest where you will meet all the clubs and sports organisations and find something to keep you busy and healthy.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything! Sports, Business/professional clubs, arts, dance and music.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Learn to dance and join a professional club if you can

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking is spectacular in the area and niagara falls is relatively close. NYC is close enough for a long weekend but expensive to stay in.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Americans are different but not difficult to live with.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Engage in activities and clubs and meet people in class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Americans are super amibitious and keep themselves busy so you can feel a little out of place if youre not

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Ambitious and intelligent students who do a lot to promote their careers.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Do it, take classes that you have an interest in, dont worry about grades(american professors are generous)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Cornell is 5 hours by bus from new york city which means you should expect to spend most of your time in Ithaca which is beautiful and fun in summer but can be a little small for winter but I didnt mind.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting other exchange students from all over the world and a few americans.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Some cultural differences meant some tension in my house. Keeping a good routine is hard when you want to get the most out of every day. Definitely plan weekend trips and perhaps plan your schedule so you have fridays or mondays or both off.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
